subject: Spike in p99 latency after v2.3 canary rollover
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@zentrihealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in p99 latency since model v2.3 rollout

Jonas / Marissa,

We started seeing a noticeable increase in p95/p99 response times this morning shortly after you finished the canary rollout to 30% of our traffic. Baseline p99 for our typical requests is ~420ms; between 08:45–09:00 PDT today it jumped to ~1.8s with a corresponding uptick in error rate (5xx ~0.9%). Throughput seemed unchanged. This is impacting our real-time triage workflows.

Can you confirm whether any config changes rolled with v2.3? We did not change request distribution or prompt sizes on our side. Please advise immediate mitigation — this is customer-visible and we risk SLA breach.

Thanks,
Sara
Ops Lead, Zentri Health

Subject: Re: Spike in p99 latency since model v2.3 rollout

Sara — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We saw anomalous telemetry from the v2.3 canary window and are escalating immediately.

Action plan (initial):
- I've looped in Engineering (David) and SRE (Stephanie) for root-cause and a fast mitigation (pause/rollback).
- We'll snapshot current canary nodes and roll traffic back to v2.2 if we confirm regression.
- I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until resolved.

Can you confirm whether any of the requests in your trace include unusually long conversation histories (tokens > 2k) or streaming flags? That will help narrow hypotheses.

—Jonas
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 10:03:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p99 latency since model v2.3 rollout

Quick summary of what we see so far from the canary nodes (10:00 snapshot):
- v2.3 introduced a slightly different KV-cache placement and an attention-kernel patch that reduces throughput for short sequence profiles but increases single-request compute in cold cache situations.
- For requests with longer histories or streaming, we see cache miss amplification that increases tail latency. Average token latency is fine; p95/p99 are pushed up by ~3–4x for affected traces.
- Error rate spike correlates with transient timeouts on canary hosts hitting a threading lock in the new runtime path — rare but visible under burst loads.

Immediate mitigations proposed:
1) Pause the v2.3 canary traffic (stop additional rollouts) and shift ongoing canary sessions back to v2.2 pool.
2) Rollback canary nodes to v2.2 or deploy a hotfix disabling the new attention-kernel path.
3) Increase canary node autoscaling buffer + bump request timeouts for canary routing while we stabilize.

I'm attaching logs and the perf snapshot we pulled. If you approve, we'll execute plan (1) now and follow with (2) unless hotfix shows immediate improvement.

—David
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
[attachment: perf_snapshot_20260315.json (json, 78KB)]

Approve the immediate pause & rollback to v2.2 for Zentri Health and any other accounts observing similar tail regressions. Notify Sales/CS to offer a one-week credit and a postmortem within 48 hours. Keep me posted on remediation timeline.

Rishi

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@zentrihealth.com>, ops@zentrihealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 14:02:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p99 latency since model v2.3 rollout

Sara — quick update and confirmation: we paused the v2.3 canary at 31% traffic and initiated an immediate rollback of canary nodes to v2.2 at 10:45 PDT yesterday. Observed effect: p99 for your traces returned from ~1.8s down to ~410–460ms within the first 12 minutes post-rollback. Error rate returned to baseline.

Next steps:
- We will run a focused regression that disables the new attention-kernel path and re-run the canary under a narrower traffic band with synthetic and your provided traces.
- Postmortem and timeline for a permanent fix will be shared within 48 hours.
- As Rishi suggested, we'll issue a one-week credit for the incident and a follow-up call to walk through findings.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this with top priority and will share logs/notes in the drive link.

Attachment: canary_logs_0315.zip (zipped logs and perf snapshots)

—Jonas
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
